text:
nisha_r: quick idea - 'burst gate' at the edge to cap cross-tenant noise. cheap preflight that enforces per-tenant fanout + latency guard, then picks a local mitigation: reduce fanout, degrade top-k, or route to smaller model. feedback?

ryan_b: sounds useful. key Q: where to store guard config? control-plane with local cache + TTL? avoids constant policy changes.

oleg: agree control-plane authoritative. implement small envelope: max_fanout, p95_ms, degrade_allowed_pct, burst_tokens. use probe refresh for heavy tenants.

nisha_r: proposal: admission runs before policy evaluation, so we don't change policy DSL. admission estimator uses histograms + headers to predict fanout; if breach -> choose mitigation via utility-aware selector. annotate request insulated=true.

infra_bot: deploy-bot: feature-flag created: edge.burstgate.v1. Canary scheduled Fri 02:00 UTC on edge-canaries.

ryan_b: tests: sim harness (1 noisy tenant), measure neighbour p95 improvement and per-tenant fallback rate + accuracy hit. add metrics: burstgate.fallbacks, burstgate.estimated_fanout.

oleg: fairness note: prefer partial mitigations (lower fanout) over opaque model swaps. add max_degrade_pct per tenant to prevent large accuracy regressions.

nisha_r: ok i'll draft RFC with envelope schema, preflight API, metrics, and canary checklist. will post in #architecture by Tue. drop thoughts here.

(end)
